name: Oman

facts.religion: Ibadi and Sunni Islam about 86%, Hindu and Christian expatriate minorities

snapshot: The Gulf's quiet mediator, an absolute monarchy that has hosted US-Iran talks and stayed out of regional wars while diversifying away from oil.
culture: Oman is the only country where most Muslims follow Ibadism, a tolerant school distinct from Sunni and Shia Islam. Its forts, frankincense trade and a seafaring history that once stretched to Zanzibar shape identity. Omani men wear the dishdasha and khanjar dagger, which is on the flag. Ancient falaj irrigation channels still water oases.
society: Oil and gas provide most revenue, but reserves are smaller than its neighbours', so Oman introduced VAT and plans the Gulf's first income tax on high earners from 2028. Omanisation policies push citizens into private jobs held by foreigners. It has a tradition of quiet diplomacy, hosting secret US-Iran talks.
baseline: Sultan Haitham bin Tarik succeeded his cousin Qaboos in 2020 and has focused on fiscal reform and an orderly succession, naming his son crown prince. Oman mediated rounds of US-Iran nuclear talks in 2025 before the war.

leaders.gov: The sultan also serves as prime minister
